quests.question: She received many job offers, most of ___ came from abroad.
quests.hint: The blank fills the slot after 'most of ___' - is the thing being referred to a group of people or a group of offers?
quests.explanation: Here 'most of ___' refers back to 'many job offers' (things), so 'which' is correct. 'Whom' would only work if referring back to a group of people.

quests.question: He interviewed twenty candidates, only two of ___ were shortlisted.
quests.hint: The blank follows 'of ___' - and the candidates are people. Which pronoun follows 'of' when referring to people?
quests.explanation: After 'of', when referring to people, 'whom' is required. 'Who' cannot follow a preposition; 'which' would be wrong because candidates are people.

quests.question: She read fifty articles, none of ___ mentioned the side effects.
quests.hint: The blank follows 'none of ___' - the articles are things, so which pronoun belongs after 'of' for things?
quests.explanation: After 'of', things take 'which'. The articles are not people, so 'whom' is incorrect; 'that' can never follow a preposition.

quests.question: The team had twelve members, three of ___ had worked together before.
quests.hint: After 'of' the blank refers back to the twelve members - people. Which form follows 'of' for people?
quests.explanation: After the preposition 'of', people require 'whom'. 'Who' cannot directly follow a preposition, and 'which' would wrongly treat the members as things.

quests.question: The company launched six products, two of ___ failed within a year.
quests.hint: After 'of' the blank refers back to products - things. Choose accordingly.
quests.explanation: After 'of', things take 'which'. Products are not people, so 'whom' is incorrect; 'that' cannot follow a preposition.

quests.question: There were ten speakers at the conference, most of ___ were experts.
quests.hint: The speakers are people, and the blank follows 'of' - apply the same rule.
quests.explanation: After the preposition 'of', people require 'whom'. 'Who' cannot follow a preposition, and 'which' would treat the speakers as things.

quests.question: We visited four museums, each of ___ had a different theme.
quests.hint: 'Each of ___' - the blank refers back to museums. Are museums people or things?
quests.explanation: Museums are things, so 'which' is required after 'of'. 'Whom' only applies to people after a preposition.

quests.question: The report named five suspects, all of ___ denied involvement.
quests.hint: 'All of ___' - the suspects are people. What form goes after 'of' for people?
quests.explanation: After 'of', when referring to people, 'whom' is required. 'Which' would wrongly treat the suspects as things.

quests.question: The store sells three coffee blends, the best of ___ comes from Ethiopia.
quests.hint: 'The best of ___' - coffee blends are things, so choose the form for things after 'of'.
quests.explanation: Coffee blends are things, so 'which' is correct after 'of'. 'That' cannot follow a preposition under any circumstances.

quests.question: I applied to eight universities, only one of ___ offered me a scholarship.
quests.hint: 'One of ___' - universities are institutions treated as things. Which pronoun follows 'of' for things?
quests.explanation: Universities are treated as things here, so 'which' follows 'of'. 'Whom' would only apply if referring back to people.

quests.question: The hospital employed thirty nurses, several of ___ had overseas training.
quests.hint: 'Several of ___' - nurses are people. Apply the 'of' + people rule.
quests.explanation: Nurses are people, so 'whom' is required after 'of'. 'Which' would wrongly treat the nurses as objects.

quests.question: The country has five major rivers, the longest of ___ flows to the sea.
quests.hint: 'The longest of ___' - rivers are things. Choose the form for things after a preposition.
quests.explanation: Rivers are things, so 'which' follows 'of'. 'That' is permanently barred from following a preposition.

quests.question: She bought several scarves, one of ___ she gave to her mother.
quests.hint: 'One of ___' - the scarves are things. What form follows 'of' for things?
quests.explanation: Scarves are things, so 'which' is correct after 'of'. 'Whom' only applies when referring to people.

quests.question: The agency hired five translators, each of ___ spoke at least three languages.
quests.hint: 'Each of ___' - translators are people. Apply the rule for people after a preposition.
quests.explanation: Translators are people, so 'whom' follows 'of'. 'Which' treats them as things; 'who' cannot follow a preposition.

quests.question: We sampled eight dishes, most of ___ were too spicy for me.
quests.hint: 'Most of ___' - dishes are things. Choose accordingly.
quests.explanation: Dishes are things, so 'which' is correct after 'of'. 'That' cannot follow a preposition.

quests.question: He forgot his keys, ___ meant he was locked out for an hour.
quests.hint: The blank doesn't refer to a specific noun - it refers back to the whole idea of forgetting his keys.
quests.explanation: When 'which' introduces a non-defining clause that comments on a whole previous idea (not just a single noun), it is called a 'comment clause'. 'That' is barred in non-defining clauses; 'what' cannot introduce this type of clause.

quests.question: The train was cancelled, ___ caused everyone to miss their connections.
quests.hint: Again, the blank refers to the entire situation described in the first clause.
quests.explanation: A comment 'which'-clause refers back to a complete idea ('the train was cancelled'). 'That' is banned in non-defining clauses; 'it' is a pronoun, not a relative connector.

quests.question: She passed her bar exam on the first attempt, ___ surprised her professors.
quests.hint: The blank points back to the whole achievement, not to a specific noun.
quests.explanation: This comment clause uses 'which' to refer to the entire preceding idea. 'That' cannot introduce a non-defining clause; 'what' would change the grammar of the sentence entirely.

quests.question: He refused to apologize, ___ made the situation much worse.
quests.hint: The blank connects back to his refusal as a whole - a comment on an entire action.
quests.explanation: Comment clauses use 'which' to refer to a complete idea from the previous clause. 'That' is barred in non-defining clauses, and 'this' is a demonstrative pronoun, not a relative connector.

quests.question: The medicine was free of charge, ___ was a huge relief.
quests.hint: The blank follows a comma and refers back to the entire situation of the medicine being free.
quests.explanation: This comment 'which' refers to the whole previous idea ('the medicine was free of charge'). 'That' cannot appear in non-defining clauses; 'it' is not a relative connector.

quests.question: They arrived three hours early, ___ turned out to be very lucky.
quests.hint: Their early arrival (the whole event) is what 'turned out to be lucky' - the blank connects to that complete idea.
quests.explanation: Comment clauses use 'which' to refer to a complete preceding idea. 'That' is barred in non-defining clauses, and 'this' is a demonstrative, not a relative pronoun.

quests.question: The power cut lasted eight hours, ___ meant the food in the fridge spoiled.
quests.hint: The whole eight-hour power cut is what caused the food to spoil - not a single noun.
quests.explanation: 'Which' in a comment clause refers back to the complete preceding idea. 'That' cannot introduce this type of clause; 'it' is a personal pronoun, not a connector.

quests.question: The prize goes to ___ wins the tournament.
quests.hint: The blank starts the subject of the sentence and refers to a person who might win - any person.
quests.explanation: 'Whoever' means 'any person who' and acts as the subject of 'wins'. 'Whatever' and 'whichever' refer to things, not people.

quests.question: You must live with ___ you decide to do.
quests.hint: The blank refers to a thing - any option or decision chosen - not a specific person or time.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever' means 'anything that' and introduces a free relative clause about a choice (a thing). 'Whoever' would refer to a person, and 'whenever'/'wherever' refer to times and places.

quests.question: She donates to ___ charity needs the most support.
quests.hint: The blank introduces a selection among multiple charities (things) - any one of them.
quests.explanation: 'Whichever' means 'any one of (these things) that' and is used when selecting from a defined set of options. 'Whoever' would only work if a person were being selected.

quests.question: You are welcome here, ___ you come from.
quests.hint: The blank introduces a place - any country or background.
quests.explanation: 'Wherever' means 'no matter where' and refers to a location. 'Whatever' refers to things; 'however' introduces manner; 'whenever' introduces time.

quests.question: She consistently achieves ___ she sets her mind to.
quests.hint: The blank introduces a thing - any goal or task she chooses to pursue.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever' means 'anything that' and here introduces a thing she sets her mind to. 'Whoever' would wrongly refer to a person.

quests.question: You can start the presentation ___ you feel ready.
quests.hint: The blank introduces a time - any moment she feels ready.
quests.explanation: 'Whenever' means 'at any time that' and introduces a free relative clause about time. 'Wherever' refers to place; 'whatever' refers to things.

quests.question: The person ___ told you that information was completely wrong.
quests.hint: The blank is the subject of 'told' and refers to an unknown person.
quests.explanation: 'Whoever' means 'any person who' and here acts as the subject of 'told'. 'Whatever' refers to things; 'however' introduces manner.

quests.question: Some people will still misunderstand, ___ carefully you explain it.
quests.hint: The blank modifies an adjective ('carefully') - it introduces a degree or manner.
quests.explanation: 'However' means 'no matter how' when it introduces an adjective or adverb. 'Whatever' refers to things; 'whoever' refers to people.
